CAUSE: `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=...)` in `app/merge_test_gate.py::run_pytest` gets `TimeoutExpired` output as bytes, even with `text=True`. The handler concatenates `exc.stdout` and `exc.stderr` with string defaults before checking whether the result is bytes. If only one stream produced output, that mixes bytes and str and raises `TypeError`; when both produced output, concatenation succeeds and the later decode runs.

I reproduced both reported error directions using the project’s Python: stdout-only timed out with `TypeError: can't concat str to bytes`; stderr-only timed out with `TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "bytes") to str`. With output on both streams, the handler succeeded.

Recommended fix: normalize each stream separately before concatenating, decoding bytes with UTF-8 and replacement, then join the resulting strings.
